abstract: Development of the next generation of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells requires assessment in systems that better recapitulate the suppressive tumour microenvironment of solid tumours. CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in of promoter-less homology directed repair templates (HDRT) into the T-cell receptor locus has been shown to result in physiological expression of CARs with improved tumour control. We initially compared the use of dsDNA and adenovirus associated virus (AAV) HDRTs in mouse T cells. We have subsequently developed an optimised method for AAV transduction resulting in high editing efficiencies with minimal toxicity. In contrast with our experience of retroviral transduction of mouse T cells, our CRISPR/Cas9 AAV transduction method results in sustained CAR expression and T cell expansion in vitro as well as in vivo persistence. This approach allows for pre-clinical assessment of individual and libraries of CAR constructs in relevant immune-competent mouse models.
